name: The Jayhawks
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Two Minneapolis rockabilly guitarists started a country-rock band in a punk town, finished a record from demos, and got signed because a producer overheard it through a phone call.

eras.title: Two rockabilly guitarists and a car wreck
eras.text: Mark Olson and Gary Louris came up in rival Minneapolis rockabilly bands, then teamed up in a country-leaning band in a city known for punk and hardcore. A car accident nearly ended it before a proper record was out.

years.h: [[Gary Louris|dd3e4c5c-b2fa-4614-9351-28362e31d015]] trades Safety Last for [[Mark Olson|51655104-6963-4a60-a7db-c2c6de58f65d]]'s band
years.p: After seeing them play in Minneapolis, Louris joins Olson, bassist [[Marc Perlman|f0e45a77-5231-4cc6-8131-27b44ff3169b]] and drummer [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]].
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com dates Louris's arrival to February 1985. Wikipedia has the band starting a year earlier as a trio of Olson, bassist Caleb Palmiter and drummer Tommy Rey, before it went four-piece and Louris replaced guitarist Steve Retzler.

Louris told Magnet that he and Olson first met when each was in a rockabilly band on the local circuit: Louris in Safety Last, Olson in Stagger Lee.

years.h: A few thousand copies on Bunkhouse, and the Burrito comparisons start
years.p: [[The Jayhawks|24ed5b09-02b1-47fe-bd83-6fa5270039b0]] press their self-titled first album for the tiny Bunkhouse label. Critics reach for the Flying Burrito Brothers.

years.src: Encyclopedia.com · Wikipedia: The Jayhawks · Wikipedia: Blue Earth
years.h: Louris is hit by a car, and the demos wait for his guitar
years.p: Encyclopedia.com describes near-fatal injuries. Wikipedia says Louris left the lineup for a stretch and came back to overdub guitar on the demos.
years.xp:
Dan Gaarder filled Louris's spot for a time, according to Wikipedia. The band was cutting demos in Minneapolis at the time, hoping to interest a bigger label.

Twin/Tone's Dave Ayers heard the tapes and suggested they be turned into an album.

eras.title: One phone call, one pile of demos
eras.text: Blue Earth started as demos and ended up a Twin/Tone record. Nobody at the label made a fuss, but a producer in Los Angeles happened to be on the line.

years.h: Twin/Tone turns a pile of demos into Blue Earth
years.p: Jim Rondinelli and Tom Herbers record in Minneapolis, and Louris returns to add guitar.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes the record was built from remixed demos cut between 1986 and 1989. Robert Christgau gave it an A-minus and called it "the obliquely songful followup the Burritos never made."

"Martin's Song" and "Two Angels" were re-recorded for Hollywood Town Hall three years later.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Jayhawks · The Current · Encyclopedia.com
years.h: Producer George Drakoulias hears Blue Earth through a phone
years.p: Calling Twin/Tone, he hears the record playing in the background, asks what it is, and signs the band to Rick Rubin's Def American label.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and The Current place the deal in 1991. Encyclopedia.com and Wikipedia tell the story the same way: Drakoulias heard the record while on the phone with the label's A&R man, Dave Ayers.

The Jayhawks had no national profile at that point. The Current describes them working the Uptown Bar, then becoming regulars at the 400 Bar on the West Bank.

eras.title: Drakoulias, twice, then Olson gets a house in Joshua Tree
eras.text: George Drakoulias made the record that put the Jayhawks in front of the rest of the country, then a bigger, costlier one. Olson walked away right after.

years.h: Hollywood Town Hall puts the Jayhawks in front of the country
years.p: Drakoulias produces, with Nicky Hopkins and Benmont Tench on keys. Pitchfork's Stephen M. Deusner later calls it "the Jayhawks' greatest statement."
years.xp:
It peaked at No. 11 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and No. 192 on the Billboard 200, Wikipedia reports. Singles were "Take Me with You (When You Go)," "Waiting for the Sun" and, in 1993, "Settled Down Like Rain."

Recording split between Hollywood Sound in Los Angeles and Pachyderm Studio in Minnesota.

years.h: [[Karen Grotberg|cdc80009-0f88-4cd9-b96b-944fe8d1c958]] arrives on keys and harmony vocals
years.p: She joins during the Hollywood Town Hall touring cycle and is a full member by the next record.

years.h: Golden Smog, a country-rock side band full of Twin Cities regulars
years.p: Louris and Perlman join Soul Asylum and Run Westy Run players for the covers EP On Golden Smog, credited under pseudonyms because of label contracts.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Golden Smog formally organized in 1989 as a country-rock reaction to the punk and hardcore that dominated the Twin Cities scene. The name comes from a Flintstones nickname for Fred Flintstone.

Its members have included Soul Asylum, Wilco and Jayhawks players; Kraig Johnson, later a Jayhawk, is a member today.

years.h: A year and a half on the road, some of it behind the Black Crowes
years.p: Encyclopedia.com says the touring won the Jayhawks new fans at rock crowds.
years.xp:
Encyclopedia.com credits the touring with making the band, and dates Tim O'Reagan's arrival on drums to 1993, in place of Ken Callahan. Wikipedia dates O'Reagan's arrival to 1995.

Perlman told the magazine the band's stuff was "too quirky and not straightforward enough" for the mainstream.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tomorrow the Green Grass · Wikipedia: The Jayhawks
years.h: Back with Drakoulias and a bigger budget for Tomorrow the Green Grass
years.p: "Blue" reaches No. 33 in Canada. "Miss Williams' Guitar" is Olson's song for Victoria Williams, his then-girlfriend.
years.xp:
It peaked at No. 92 on the Billboard 200, Wikipedia reports. Don Heffington played drums on the album; Benmont Tench and violinist Lili Haydn guested.

Wikipedia says US sales disappointed given the cost of the production.

q: It wasn't a joyous ride, man.
years.h: Olson quits for Joshua Tree and Victoria Williams
years.p: He says he'd just married, found a house there and wanted to try something else. Louris tells Magnet Olson was tired of radio promotion.
years.xp:
Olson went on to make sparse, living-room records with Williams as the Original Harmony Ridge Creekdippers, taping some vocals in the bathroom, he told PopMatters. Paste quotes him on the change: "just became a different person."

Tim O'Reagan was already the drummer and a second vocalist; Kraig Johnson came in on guitar.

eras.title: Louris takes the wheel
eras.text: Without Olson, Louris wrote most of the songs and pushed toward psych, pop and power chords. Fans still argue over which Jayhawks they prefer.

years.h: Louris takes the songwriting lead on Sound of Lies
years.p: Straight rock, psychedelia and acoustic songs, with Kraig Johnson on guitar for the first time.
years.xp: Louris told Magnet his inspirations were Brian Eno, the Clash, the Kinks and the Beatles more than country records. Little Village reports that the fanbase has divided since Sound of Lies over which era was better.

years.big: "What If You Made a Classic, and No One Cared?"
years.h: Bob Ezrin and drum loops arrive with Smile
years.p: The New York Times ran its warm review of the record under that headline.
years.xp: Grotberg, pregnant, left before the tour and Jen Gunderman replaced her. "I'm Gonna Make You Love Me" ended up in Ralph Lauren commercials and on the Dawson's Creek Volume 2 soundtrack, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Louris drives to Joshua Tree, and the writing starts again
years.p: Olson told Elsewhere that in 2001 Louris came to his place and they wrote together for the first time in years.
years.xp: Louris told Magnet the thaw began with a request to write for the Dennis Quaid film The Rookie. He drove to Joshua Tree and they "talked through our old issues." Olson and Louris began touring together intermittently from 2001, per Paste.

years.h: Rainy Day Music goes acoustic and heads back toward country
years.p: Pedal steel and banjo from [[Stephen McCarthy|850adef3-13a0-4206-9126-44c5abbefaaf]] of the Long Ryders, and the band plays Austin City Limits for the first time.

years.h: The last show is in Valencia, Spain, then nothing as a band
years.p: Wikipedia says the band stopped after touring Rainy Day Music, ending in Valencia.

eras.title: The hawks come back, and Olson leaves again
eras.text: Olson and Louris toured as a duo, then the mid-90s lineup returned for festivals, a box of rarities and one new record. It didn't last.

years.cap: Olson and Louris, Union Chapel, London
years.h: Olson and Louris go out as a duo, billed "From the Jayhawks"
years.p: The tour is titled "From the Jayhawks: An Evening with Mark Olson & Gary Louris, Together Again."
years.xp: Olson told PopMatters that they enjoyed writing songs that way and wanted people to hear how they sounded when first written. That became Ready for the Flood, released in January 2009 per Wikipedia (Olson dates the recording to 2008).

years.h: The 1995 lineup returns, first in Barcelona, then in Minneapolis
years.p: Louris, Olson, Perlman, Grotberg and O'Reagan play Primavera Sound in Barcelona on May 30 and the Basilica Block Party in Minneapolis on July 10.
years.xp:
Billboard reported the reunion in April 2009. Louris said the plan was to play festivals, and hoped for Bonnaroo the year after.

Paste dates a one-off at Spain's Azkena Rock Festival to September 2009; Wikipedia's timeline says 2008 in one place and 2009 in another.

years.h: Sony Legacy opens the vault with Music from the North Country
years.p: Louris supervises the anthology of highlights, B-sides, rarities and videos.
years.xp: Paste says compiling the anthology helped inspire the full lineup's return.

years.h: Webster Hall hears both albums front to back, two nights running
years.p: The reunited five play Hollywood Town Hall on January 20 and Tomorrow the Green Grass on January 21, part of a Toronto-to-Minneapolis run.
years.xp: Legacy had just reissued both albums as collector's editions, with the Mystery Demos disc of 1992 recordings by Olson and Louris. The mini-tour also hit Philadelphia, Chicago and Minneapolis.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mockingbird Time · Wikipedia: The Jayhawks
years.h: Mockingbird Time puts Olson back on a Jayhawks record
years.p: Louris produces at the Terrarium in Minneapolis, November 5 to December 4, 2010. It enters the Billboard 200 at No. 38.
years.xp: They wrote in Louris's apartment, at Olson's Joshua Tree home and in a cabin in northern Minnesota, and cut 18 songs, 16 of them new. AllMusic's Mark Deming called it the strongest since Hollywood Town Hall.

years.h: Olson walks out a second time after the Mockingbird Time tour
years.p: Wikipedia's page for the record says Olson complained about money and songwriting credits. Louris called it "a fiasco" that left a bad taste.
years.xp: Little Village reports Olson cited personal differences and band business, and that Louris was being treated for painkiller addiction at the time. Louris told Rolling Stone Country it took getting clean and sober to appreciate what he had, including the Jayhawks.

eras.title: Four voices, no frontman
eras.text: Without Olson, Louris turned the band into a group of songwriters and singers, working with R.E.M.'s Peter Buck and the Kinks' Ray Davies.

years.h: Reissues send the late-90s lineup back on the road
years.p: Deluxe editions of Sound of Lies, Smile and Rainy Day Music get the band playing songs it hadn't touched in a decade.
years.xp: The two-LP editions were remastered by Vic Anesini; Smile got its first U.S. vinyl release.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paging Mr. Proust · Little Village
years.h: Paging Mr. Proust is cut in Portland with Peter Buck and Tucker Martine
years.p: Three songs are full-band co-writes. Louris said he wanted to feature three good vocalists.
years.xp: It peaked at No. 75 on the Billboard 200. Kraig Johnson left before release and John Jackson, who played on it, joined the touring band.

years.h: Tiny Desk at NPR's offices, stripped down
years.p: The Jayhawks play a short set behind a desk. NPR Music dates it August 5, 2016.

yt: Ray Davies & the Jayhawks, "Wings of Fantasy"
years.h: Ray Davies makes an Americana record with the Jayhawks behind him
years.p: The former Kinks singer records his U.S. memoir album with the band, then a follow-up, Our Country: Americana Act II, in 2018.

years.h: Norm Rogers, the original drummer, dies of cancer
years.p: Wikipedia lists him as the band's drummer from 1984 to 1988.

years.h: John Jackson joins as a fifth member for Back Roads and Abandoned Motels
years.p: Sony Legacy releases it, with Jackson also co-producing.

years.h: XOXO hands the lead vocal around
years.p: Louris, Perlman, O'Reagan and Grotberg each sing lead on songs. The band plays CBS This Morning: Saturday on June 27.

years.h: The First Avenue wall gives the Jayhawks a star
years.p: The Minneapolis club puts the band on its outside mural. Journalist Steve Marsh called it possibly the city's most prestigious public honor for an artist.
years.xp: Stars go to acts with sold-out shows or significant cultural contribution to the club.
